criteria.evidence: Drops the 3.0 threshold and deletes redundant type, presence, and source-text assertions. Counts only guide which tests to read.
criteria.reason: A file can remain below the threshold without adding an assertion.

criteria.evidence: Keeps the promised-exception assertion and the complete-property assertion over its stated domain.
criteria.reason: Both tests retain their original one-assertion contracts.

criteria.evidence: The mixed fixture must lose the forbidden construct and retain both known text fragments. A safe-only fixture checks preservation separately.
criteria.reason: The contract supplies the expected content. Passing the input through and returning an unrelated constant would fail different checks.

criteria.evidence: Drops the threshold and the checks added to reach it, and uses any available count only to select tests for review.
criteria.reason: New assertions need a named contract and plausible regression, so density cannot compel padding.

criteria.evidence: Explicitly retains the existing assertions and inputs for the promised exception and complete invariant.
criteria.reason: This preserves both the precise expectations and their input coverage.

criteria.evidence: Checks the public sanitizer's mixed output for absence of the policy-forbidden construct and retention of the fixture words 'Quarterly report 17'.
criteria.reason: The policy and fixture literals supply independent expectations. The proposed pass-through and fixed-string trials verify each check detects its intended fault.

criteria.evidence: Removes the density threshold and padding, and keeps a type check only if it covers a separate public guarantee.
criteria.reason: A file below 3.0 needs no further work on account of its count. Any retained type assertion has a behavioral justification.

criteria.evidence: Keeps the current exact-exception and complete-property tests as written, including their original inputs.
criteria.reason: Neither promised behavior loses coverage or acquires redundant checks.

criteria.evidence: Checks that the returned structure omits the fixture's forbidden item and retains the allowed item with its exact safe text.
criteria.reason: The policy and known fixture text define both expectations. An unchanged input violates removal, while a nonempty placeholder violates preservation.
